title: Shader Fields, Gap Rules, Melting Type, Haptics & Native Sliders
description: Five fresh drops: a WebGL cursor-displaced shader field, native CSS gap-gutter dividers, a gooey melting headline, real device haptics, and a preview native dual-thumb range group.

drops.title: Cursor Shader Field
drops.description: A procedurally generated image dissolves into a live grid of GPU point-sprites that ripple, push outward, and glow as the cursor sweeps across.
drops.concept: A colorful abstract image is painted onto an offscreen 2D canvas (no external asset needed), then sampled pixel-by-pixel to build one point per grid cell in a raw WebGL point-sprite mesh — each vertex carries its base UV position plus the sampled RGB as attributes. The vertex shader receives the cursor position as a uniform; distance-to-cursor drives a radial outward displacement and a size/glow boost, and the fragment shader renders each point as a soft round sprite blended additively so the field glows near the cursor and settles elsewhere.
drops.source: Gabriel Villanueva — "Particles Cursor Turns Images Into a Shader Field" (webgpu.com showcase)

interaction.mouse: Move the cursor across the field — nearby points push outward and glow
interaction.click: Use the debug panel's Regenerate button for a new procedural art seed
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across the canvas on mobile to displace the field

drops.title: Gap Rule Grid
drops.description: A bento grid grows real divider lines directly inside its gutters via the proposed column-rule/row-rule gap-decoration properties — no divider elements.
drops.concept: CSS Gap Decorations extend the familiar multi-column column-rule idea to 2D grid and flexbox gaps in both axes: column-rule-style/-width/-color paint vertical gutter lines, row-rule-* paint horizontal ones, all without any extra markup. Since support is still emerging, a live CSS.supports() check reports the real status in a badge, and when the native properties aren't recognized, JS measures each grid item's bounding box to compute exact gap-line positions and paints an absolutely-positioned overlay — visually identical, degrading gracefully on any browser.
drops.source: web.dev — "New to the web platform in June" (Chrome CSS Gap Decorations roundup)

interaction.mouse: Drag the gap/width sliders and change the rule style/color in the debug panel
interaction.click: Switch the rule style dropdown to see dashed/dotted/double variants
interaction.touch: Panel hides on small screens; grid itself is fully responsive

drops.title: Melt Type
drops.description: Headline letters slump and drip downward like warm wax, using nothing but a chained SVG filter and a per-letter keyframe loop.
drops.concept: A classic 'gooey' SVG filter chain — feGaussianBlur softens each glyph's edges, feColorMatrix cranks the alpha contrast to re-fuse that blur into a sharp, fused edge, and feOffset biases the result slightly downward before compositing back over the source — is applied via filter:url(#id) to a headline split into per-letter spans. Each span runs its own staggered @keyframes loop that stretches it downward and back, so the goo filter and the animation together read as continuous dripping wax rather than a single melt.

interaction.mouse: Hover the headline to slow the drip way down; drag sliders to change drip depth, speed and goo blur
interaction.click: Pause/resume button freezes the melt entirely
interaction.touch: Sliders hidden on small screens; animation runs automatically

drops.title: Haptic Taps
drops.description: Buttons fire genuine navigator.vibrate() patterns on supporting devices, paired with a visible pulse-ring and shake so the timing reads everywhere else.
drops.concept: Four named presets (success, nudge, error, buzz) map to distinct millisecond vibration patterns passed straight to navigator.vibrate(pattern[]). Because most desktops and iOS Safari have no Vibration API, every tap also fires a synchronized CSS pulse-ring and shake animation whose duration matches the real pattern's total length, so the feel of each preset is visible even without hardware — a live badge and a status log report whether the real API actually fired or the simulation ran instead.
drops.source: Lochie — web-haptics npm package (Vibration API presets)

interaction.mouse: Click any preset button to fire its pattern and watch the pulse ring
interaction.click: Same as mouse — every preset is a button
interaction.touch: Tap on a real phone with Vibration API support to feel the actual pattern

drops.title: Native Dual Slider
drops.description: A working preview of the proposed native <rangegroup> element — two synced range thumbs with a colored fill segment between them and an enforced minimum gap.
drops.concept: The OpenUI/CSSWG 'Enhanced Range Input' explainer proposes a <rangegroup> wrapper holding two <input type=range> children with a stepbetween attribute enforcing a minimum gap, plus new ::slider-track/::slider-thumb/::slider-fill/::slider-segment(n) pseudo-elements for styling each zone. No browser ships this yet, so this drop simulates it faithfully: two native range inputs are layered with a JS-computed absolutely-positioned fill bar recoloring the below/between/above zones, and an input handler clamps the thumbs to the configured minimum gap — degrading to two fully independent, functional sliders if JS ever fails.
drops.source: Open UI — "Enhanced Range Input" component explainer (rangegroup proposal)
tech: CSS custom properties for fill math

interaction.mouse: Drag either thumb — the fill segment and readouts update live, and thumbs can't cross the minimum gap
interaction.click: Adjust the minimum-gap slider in the debug panel to feel the clamp change
interaction.touch: Thumbs are touch-draggable; native range inputs get full mobile support for free
